geographic_flags.quote: Director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad released both series in Putrajaya on 31 July 2026.
geographic_flags.why_biased: Frames the issue strictly from a federal administrative lens, omitting that industrial fires are heavily concentrated in specific manufacturing states like Selangor and Johor, which bear the actual geographic and resource risk.
geographic_flags.fix: Acknowledge the regional concentration of these industrial fires, specifically citing high-risk states like Selangor as contextualized by JBPM's broader national data.

economic_flags.quote: Factories were about 2.9 per cent of the structure and vehicle fires JBPM reported for 2025, and about 36.9 per cent of the losses
economic_flags.why_biased: Evaluates the severity of factory fires strictly through the lens of capital loss (RM770.69 million) and property destruction, completely masking the human labor cost by omitting worker safety or casualties.
economic_flags.fix: Include data or context regarding worker casualties, injuries, or the occupational safety impact of these industrial fires, as national structural fire data tracks fatalities.

omission_flags: Institutional Monoculture: The analysis relies exclusively on government and regulatory sources (JBPM, NADMA, AGC), completely omitting the perspective, financial burden, and compliance efforts of the manufacturing industry itself (e.g., FMM seminars on OKK compliance), as well as labor unions and insurance underwriters.
Human Cost: Fails to mention the number of worker casualties or injuries associated with the 2,001 factory fires, masking the human impact of the disasters.
evasion_flags: Self-Regulatory Risks: The analysis notes the shift toward internal tests prepared inside the building but evades a critical assessment of the conflict of interest, compliance friction, and systemic risks inherent in corporate self-regulation of fire safety.

cardinal_sin_flags.quote: 463 factory fires, up 28.6 per cent, alongside 1,191 hazard notices against 706 the year before.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: While factually accurate to media reports of the Director-General's speech, these specific 2025 figures are drawn from oral remarks reported in the press rather than a published, auditable statistical report or JBPM table.
cardinal_sin_flags.fix: Explicitly state that these figures were cited during a speech or monthly assembly and reported by the media, rather than derived from an officially published dataset.

verification_log.claim: JBPM reported 2,001 factory fires and RM4.21 billion lost over six years
JBPM reported 1,878 factory inspections in 2025 against 1,563 in 2024
Inspections rose 20.2 per cent, notices 68.7 per cent
JBPM put 2025 structure and vehicle fires at 16,111, costing RM2.09 billion
verification_log.primary_source: Kosmo Digital / NADMA portal, 20 Jan 2026 (Datuk Ahmad Izram Osman)

verification_log.claim: Section 27 of the Fire Services Act 1988 lets the Director General designate premises
section 28 requires a fire certificate for designated premises, renewable annually
section 33 makes use without one an offence carrying up to RM50,000, up to five years' imprisonment, or both
The designated-premises order sets factory thresholds by floor area, storeys and use
2020 fire certificate regulations already required a fire safety organization with a registered fire safety manager and officers
What Nor Hisham announced on 4 August 2025
The amendment behind it commenced in phases, with specified provisions from 1 January 2026
JBPM reported 222 factory fires from January to June 2026

overall_assessment: The v2 analysis is factually accurate regarding the metrics and statutory framework cited by government sources, demonstrating commendable restraint against overclaiming causal links. However, it suffers from a severe institutional monoculture. By relying solely on JBPM and state media, it completely ignores the operational burden on the manufacturing sector (e.g., FMM compliance efforts) and exhibits an economic masking bias by framing industrial fire disasters strictly in terms of capital losses (RM billions) while entirely omitting worker casualties and localized impacts in highly industrialized states.
